# @ndigo/ui

Ndigo UI — brand tokens, theme layers, and the design-system registry contract

Version-matched export index for the installed package. Read `README.md`
for usage; the workspace guide index ships with `@ndigo/cli` as
`assets/agent/docs-index.md`.

## Subpaths

- `@ndigo/ui/tokens.css`
- `@ndigo/ui/theme.css`

## Public exports

- `getTokenDefinition` — Looks up the catalog definition for a token name.
- `TOKEN_NAMES` — Every token name in the catalog, in declaration order.
- `TOKENS`
- `TokenDefinition` *(type)* — Catalog entry for one design token.
- `TOKEN_GROUPS` — Stable token groups shared by the catalog, documentation, and drift checks.
- `TokenGroup` *(type)* — One of the stable token groups.
- `TokenName` *(type)* — Canonical token-name type for ndigo-ui.
- `resolveToken` — Builds a `var()` reference for a token, optionally with a fallback.
- `Theme` *(type)* — A named theme: an identity, a color scheme, and its token overrides.
- `ThemeColorScheme` *(type)* — Light or dark presentation of a theme.
- `ThemeTokens` *(type)* — Partial map of design-token names to override values for a theme.
- `createTheme` — Creates a theme, inheriting tokens from a base theme when provided.
- `withThemeTokens` — Returns a copy of `theme` with additional token overrides merged in.
- `CreateThemeOptions` *(type)* — Options for createTheme.
- `applyTheme` — Applies a theme to `target`, replacing any previously applied theme.
- `removeTheme` — Removes an applied theme from `target`, clearing inline overrides and the theme attributes.
- `ThemeTarget` *(type)* — Minimal structural shape of a theming target, so this module does not depend on DOM type declarations.
- `themeToCss` — Builds a CSS rule that applies a theme's token overrides to `selector`.
- `resolveVisualTheme` — Resolves a negotiated theme name to a visual theme.
- `VisualThemeMap` *(type)* — Application-supplied map of theme names to themes.
- `themeAttributes` — Builds the HTML attributes for a theme.
- `ThemeAttributes` *(type)* — Attributes that select a theme in server-rendered markup.
- `COMMON_THEMES`
- `getCommonTheme` — Finds a built-in theme by name.
- `HIGH_CONTRAST_DARK_THEME`
- `HIGH_CONTRAST_LIGHT_THEME`
- `NDIGO_DARK_THEME`
- `NDIGO_LIGHT_THEME`
- `SOLARIZED_DARK_THEME`
- `SOLARIZED_LIGHT_THEME`
